title: Drawing in perspective
examples: Teacher, what is the horizon line really?
Can you show me where the vanishing point goes?
How do I make my drawing look like it's far away?

explain.say: Today we are learning about drawing in perspective. Perspective makes your drawings look real. It makes things look three dimensional.
First we need to draw the horizon line. This line represents your eye level. Imagine looking across a calm lake.
Next we find the vanishing point. This point sits right on the horizon line. It is where parallel lines appear to meet.
Now we use one-point perspective. This means all lines go toward one point. The vanishing point is that one point.
Look at a road stretching into the distance. The edges of the road seem to meet at one point. That is a perfect real-life example.

draw.text: Real Life: Roads meeting a point

explain.say: A common mistake is drawing everything at the same size. Remember that things far away must look smaller. Always check your lines meet the point.

draw.text: Mistake: Objects staying the same size

faq.q: What is the difference between the horizon line and the vanishing point?
faq.a: The horizon line is a straight line showing your eye level. The vanishing point is a single spot that sits directly on that line.
asks: Where do I put the vanishing point?
Is the vanishing point always on the horizon line?

faq.q: Do I need a vanishing point for every drawing?
faq.a: No, you only need one if you are drawing parallel lines receding into the distance. You can use other methods too.
asks: When should I use perspective drawing?

faq.q: If I am drawing a very tall building, where is my horizon line?
faq.a: If you are looking up at a very tall building, your horizon line will be low. If you are looking down, it will be high.
asks: Does my viewpoint change the line?
How high should the line be?

faq.q: What if I draw a square but it looks like a trapezoid?
faq.a: This usually means your lines are not correctly aimed at the vanishing point. Check that all sides are pointing to that single spot.
asks: My box looks crooked, what did I do wrong?
How do I make my square look straight from far away?

faq.q: Can I use this technique for drawing people?
faq.a: Perspective is best for straight, receding lines like roads or train tracks. People are more complex shapes.
asks: Can I use this for a person standing on a street?

facts: The horizon line represents the level of the viewer's eyes.
The vanishing point is the spot where parallel lines appear to meet.
One-point perspective uses only one vanishing point for all receding lines.
Objects appear smaller the further away they are from the viewer.

quiz.say: If you are standing on a beach looking out at the ocean, where is your horizon line?
quiz.why: When looking at a wide view like the ocean, your eye level is usually low.

wrong.0: The horizon line is a horizontal line across the middle.
wrong.1: The horizon line always exists based on your eye level.
wrong.3: This would mean you are looking down from a very high place.

quiz.say: What must all the parallel lines in a one-point perspective drawing point towards?
quiz.show: A. The corner of the paper

options.show: A. The corner of the paper
options.say: A. The corner of the paper

options.show: C. The center of the page
options.say: C. The center of the page

quiz.why: The vanishing point is the single spot where all receding parallel lines appear to meet.

wrong.0: The top edge is not where receding lines converge.
wrong.2: Corners are for drawing shapes, not for where lines meet.
wrong.3: The center is too general; it must be a specific point.

quiz.say: If you draw a row of railroad tracks, what must you do to make them look correct?
quiz.show: A. Keep them all the same length

options.show: B. Make them get smaller towards a point
options.say: B. Make them get smaller towards a point

options.show: A. Keep them all the same length
options.say: A. Keep them all the same length

options.show: D. Draw them parallel to the edge
options.say: D. Draw them parallel to the edge

quiz.why: Perspective requires that objects get progressively smaller as they move away from you.

wrong.1: This makes the drawing look flat and unrealistic.
wrong.2: Curving them up changes the perspective entirely.
wrong.3: Parallel lines must appear to meet at a point in perspective.
